title: How does caffeine keep us awake? - Hanan Qasim
speaker: TED-Ed
zh: 【TED-Ed】咖啡因如何讓我們保持清醒？ ——哈南·卡西姆（精選雙語跟讀教材）

cues.text: Over 100,000 metric tons of caffeine are consumed
cues.en: Over 100,000 metric tons of caffeine are consumed
cues.zh: 全世界每年消耗了超過

cues.text: around the world every year.
cues.en: around the world every year.
cues.zh: 全世界每年消耗了超過 十萬公噸的咖啡因

cues.text: That's equivalent to the weight of 14 Eiffel Towers.
cues.en: That's equivalent to the weight of 14 Eiffel Towers.
cues.zh: 十萬公噸的咖啡因 這相當於十四座艾菲爾鐵塔的重量

cues.text: Most of this caffeine is consumed in coffee and tea, but it's also ingested in some sodas,
cues.en: Most of this caffeine is consumed in coffee and tea, but it's also ingested in some sodas,
cues.zh: 這相當於十四座艾菲爾鐵塔的重量 其中大部分咖啡因消耗於咖啡和茶 但也會被攝取自某些汽水 巧克力

cues.text: chocolate, caffeine pills, and even beverages labeled decaf.
cues.en: chocolate, caffeine pills, and even beverages labeled decaf.
cues.zh: 巧克力 咖啡因藥丸 甚至標示為無咖啡因的飲料

cues.text: Caffeine helps us feel alert, focused, happy, and energetic,
cues.en: Caffeine helps us feel alert, focused, happy, and energetic,
cues.zh: 甚至標示為無咖啡因的飲料 咖啡因幫助我們感到警戒 專注、快樂、並充滿活力 即使我們沒有睡飽

cues.text: even if we haven't had enough sleep.
cues.en: even if we haven't had enough sleep.
cues.zh: 即使我們沒有睡飽

cues.text: But it can also raise our blood pressure, and make us feel anxious.
cues.en: But it can also raise our blood pressure, and make us feel anxious.
cues.zh: 即使我們沒有睡飽 但它也能夠升高我們的血壓 並讓我們感到焦慮

cues.text: It's the world most widely used drug.
cues.en: It's the world most widely used drug.
cues.zh: 但它也能夠升高我們的血壓 並讓我們感到焦慮 這是世界上使用最廣的藥物

cues.text: So how does it keep us awake?
cues.en: So how does it keep us awake?
cues.zh: 這是世界上使用最廣的藥物 所以它如何使我們醒著呢

cues.text: Caffeine evolved in plants where it serves a few purposes.
cues.en: Caffeine evolved in plants where it serves a few purposes.
cues.zh: 所以它如何使我們醒著呢 咖啡因在植物中演化 扮演著幾個角色

cues.text: In high doses, as it's found in the leaves and seeds of certain species,
cues.en: In high doses, as it's found in the leaves and seeds of certain species,
cues.zh: 咖啡因在植物中演化 扮演著幾個角色 高劑量咖啡因 如同在某些物種的 葉子及種子中能找到的

cues.text: it's toxic to insects.
cues.en: it's toxic to insects.
cues.zh: 如同在某些物種的 葉子及種子中能找到的 對昆蟲有毒性

cues.text: But when they consume it in lower doses, as it's found in nectar,
cues.en: But when they consume it in lower doses, as it's found in nectar,
cues.zh: 對昆蟲有毒性 但當牠們攝取低劑量時 如同花蜜中能找到的

cues.text: it can actually help them remember and revisit flowers.
cues.en: it can actually help them remember and revisit flowers.
cues.zh: 但當牠們攝取低劑量時 如同花蜜中能找到的 咖啡因實際上可以幫助牠們 記住並重返花朵

cues.text: In the human body, caffeine acts as a stimulant for the central nervous system.
cues.en: In the human body, caffeine acts as a stimulant for the central nervous system.
cues.zh: 在人體內，咖啡因作為一種 中樞神經興奮劑

cues.text: It keeps us awake by blocking one of the body's key sleep-inducing molecules,
cues.en: It keeps us awake by blocking one of the body's key sleep-inducing molecules,
cues.zh: 在人體內，咖啡因作為一種 中樞神經興奮劑 它藉由阻斷體內其中一種 誘發睡眠的關鍵分子而使我們醒著

cues.text: a substance called adenosine.
cues.en: a substance called adenosine.
cues.zh: 它藉由阻斷體內其中一種 誘發睡眠的關鍵分子而使我們醒著 一種叫做腺苷的物質

cues.text: Your body needs a constant supply of energy, which it gets by breaking down a high-energy molecule called ATP.
cues.en: Your body needs a constant supply of energy, which it gets by breaking down a high-energy molecule called ATP.
cues.zh: 一種叫做腺苷的物質 你的身體需要穩定的能量供應 藉由分解一種叫三磷酸腺核苷 的高能分子而得到

cues.text: In the process, it liberates adenosine, ATP's chemical backbone.
cues.en: In the process, it liberates adenosine, ATP's chemical backbone.
cues.zh: 藉由分解一種叫三磷酸腺核苷 的高能分子而得到 在過程中 它釋出腺苷 就是 ATP 的化學結構骨架

cues.text: Neurons in your brain have receptors perfectly tailored to this molecule.
cues.en: Neurons in your brain have receptors perfectly tailored to this molecule.
cues.zh: 它釋出腺苷 就是 ATP 的化學結構骨架 你腦中的神經元 有為這種分子量身打造的受體

cues.text: When adenosine docks to these receptors, it activates a cascade of biochemical reactions
cues.en: When adenosine docks to these receptors, it activates a cascade of biochemical reactions
cues.zh: 你腦中的神經元 有為這種分子量身打造的受體 當腺苷停泊於受體時 它會活化一連串的生化反應

cues.text: that cause neurons to fire more sluggishly and slow the release of important brain-signaling molecules.
cues.en: that cause neurons to fire more sluggishly and slow the release of important brain-signaling molecules.
cues.zh: 它會活化一連串的生化反應 使得神經元較慵懶地放電 並減緩重要大腦傳訊分子的釋放

cues.text: In other words, you get sleepy.
cues.en: In other words, you get sleepy.
cues.zh: 並減緩重要大腦傳訊分子的釋放 換句話說，你會感到想睡

cues.text: Caffeine is what's called an adenosine receptor antagonist.
cues.en: Caffeine is what's called an adenosine receptor antagonist.
cues.zh: 換句話說，你會感到想睡 咖啡因是所謂的腺苷受體拮抗劑

cues.text: That means it derails this process of slowing your neurons down
cues.en: That means it derails this process of slowing your neurons down
cues.zh: 咖啡因是所謂的腺苷受體拮抗劑 意思是咖啡因會藉由阻斷腺苷受體 來阻止使神經元變遲緩的過程

cues.text: by blocking adenosine receptors.
cues.en: by blocking adenosine receptors.
cues.zh: 來阻止使神經元變遲緩的過程

cues.text: Caffeine and adenosine have a similar molecular structure, close enough that caffeine can wedge into the adenosine receptors,
cues.en: Caffeine and adenosine have a similar molecular structure, close enough that caffeine can wedge into the adenosine receptors,
cues.zh: 咖啡因和腺苷有相似的分子結構 接近到咖啡因可以卡進腺苷受體中

cues.text: but not close enough to activate them.
cues.en: but not close enough to activate them.
cues.zh: 接近到咖啡因可以卡進腺苷受體中 但沒有接近到能夠活化受體

cues.text: To summarize, adenosine inhibits your neurons.
cues.en: To summarize, adenosine inhibits your neurons.
cues.zh: 總結來說，腺苷抑制你的神經元

cues.text: Caffeine inhibits the inhibitor, so it stimulates you.
cues.en: Caffeine inhibits the inhibitor, so it stimulates you.
cues.zh: 咖啡因抑制了抑制劑，所以它刺激你

cues.text: Caffeine can also boost positive feelings.
cues.en: Caffeine can also boost positive feelings.
cues.zh: 咖啡因抑制了抑制劑，所以它刺激你 咖啡因也能促進正向的感覺

cues.text: In some neurons, the adenosine receptors are linked to receptors for another molecule called dopamine.
cues.en: In some neurons, the adenosine receptors are linked to receptors for another molecule called dopamine.
cues.zh: 在某些神經元中 腺苷受體與另一種叫 多巴胺的分子之受體連線

cues.text: One of dopamine's roles in the brain is to promote feelings of pleasure.
cues.en: One of dopamine's roles in the brain is to promote feelings of pleasure.
cues.zh: 腺苷受體與另一種叫 多巴胺的分子之受體連線 多巴胺在腦中的其中一個角色 是提升愉悅感

cues.text: When adenosine docks in one of these paired receptors, that can make it harder for dopamine to fit in its own spot,
cues.en: When adenosine docks in one of these paired receptors, that can make it harder for dopamine to fit in its own spot,
cues.zh: 當腺苷停泊在這些 成對受體中的一個時 會使多巴胺較難結合到自己的位置上

cues.text: interrupting its mood-lifting work.
cues.en: interrupting its mood-lifting work.
cues.zh: 會使多巴胺較難結合到自己的位置上 便幹擾了它提升心情的作用

cues.text: But when caffeine takes adenosine's place, it doesn't have the same effect,
cues.en: But when caffeine takes adenosine's place, it doesn't have the same effect,
cues.zh: 便幹擾了它提升心情的作用 但當咖啡因取代腺苷的位置時 它不會有相同的作用

cues.text: and dopamine can slide in.
cues.en: and dopamine can slide in.
cues.zh: 但當咖啡因取代腺苷的位置時 它不會有相同的作用 並且多巴胺可以滑進來

cues.text: There's evidence that caffeine's effects on adenosine and dopamine receptors
cues.en: There's evidence that caffeine's effects on adenosine and dopamine receptors
cues.zh: 有證據顯示咖啡因 對腺苷和多巴胺受體的作用

cues.text: can have long-term benefits, too, reducing the risk of diseases
cues.en: can have long-term benefits, too, reducing the risk of diseases
cues.zh: 也可能對於減少某些疾病 有長期的益處

cues.text: like Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and some types of cancer.
cues.en: like Parkinson's, Alzheimer's, and some types of cancer.
cues.zh: 像是帕金森氏症、阿茲海默症 和某些型別的癌症

cues.text: Caffeine can also ramp up the body's ability to burn fat.
cues.en: Caffeine can also ramp up the body's ability to burn fat.
cues.zh: 咖啡因也能提升身體燃燒脂肪的能力

cues.text: In fact, some sports organizations think that caffeine gives athletes an unfair advantage
cues.en: In fact, some sports organizations think that caffeine gives athletes an unfair advantage
cues.zh: 咖啡因也能提升身體燃燒脂肪的能力 事實上，有些運動協會認為 咖啡因給予運動員不公平的優勢

cues.text: and have placed limits on its consumption.
cues.en: and have placed limits on its consumption.
cues.zh: 咖啡因給予運動員不公平的優勢 並已對咖啡因的使用設下限制

cues.text: From 1972 until 2004, Olympic athletes had to stay below a certain blood-caffeine concentration
cues.en: From 1972 until 2004, Olympic athletes had to stay below a certain blood-caffeine concentration
cues.zh: 並已對咖啡因的使用設下限制 從 1972 年到 2004 年 奧運選手的血中咖啡因 必須保持在某特定濃度之下

cues.text: to compete.
cues.en: to compete.
cues.zh: 奧運選手的血中咖啡因 必須保持在某特定濃度之下 才能比賽

cues.text: Of course, not all of caffeine's effects are so helpful.
cues.en: Of course, not all of caffeine's effects are so helpful.
cues.zh: 才能比賽 當然咖啡因的作用不全是有幫助的

cues.text: It might make you feel better and more alert, but it can also raise your heart rate and blood pressure,
cues.en: It might make you feel better and more alert, but it can also raise your heart rate and blood pressure,
cues.zh: 當然咖啡因的作用不全是有幫助的 它可能會讓你感覺較好，並較警覺 但它也能升高你的心率和血壓

cues.text: cause increased urination or diarrhea, and contribute to insomnia and anxiety.
cues.en: cause increased urination or diarrhea, and contribute to insomnia and anxiety.
cues.zh: 造成多尿或腹瀉 並引起失眠和焦慮

cues.text: Plus, the foods and beverages caffeine is found in have their own impacts on your body that have to be taken into account.
cues.en: Plus, the foods and beverages caffeine is found in have their own impacts on your body that have to be taken into account.
cues.zh: 並引起失眠和焦慮 此外，含有咖啡因的食物和飲料 它們本身對你身體的影響 也必須列入考慮

cues.text: Your brain can adapt to regular consumption of caffeine.
cues.en: Your brain can adapt to regular consumption of caffeine.
cues.zh: 它們本身對你身體的影響 也必須列入考慮 你的大腦可以適應規律的咖啡因攝取

cues.text: If your adenosine receptors are perpetually clogged, your body will manufacture extra ones.
cues.en: If your adenosine receptors are perpetually clogged, your body will manufacture extra ones.
cues.zh: 你的大腦可以適應規律的咖啡因攝取 如果你的腺苷受體被長期堵塞 你的身體會額外製造

cues.text: That way, even with caffeine around, adenosine can still do its job of signaling the brain to power down.
cues.en: That way, even with caffeine around, adenosine can still do its job of signaling the brain to power down.
cues.zh: 你的身體會額外製造 這樣一來，即使有咖啡因存在 腺苷還是能做它傳訊 使大腦省電的工作

cues.text: That's why you may find you need to consume more and more caffeine
cues.en: That's why you may find you need to consume more and more caffeine
cues.zh: 腺苷還是能做它傳訊 使大腦省電的工作 這就是為什麼你可能會發覺 你需要消耗越來越多的咖啡因 以感受到相同的警覺

cues.text: to feel as alert.
cues.en: to feel as alert.
cues.zh: 以感受到相同的警覺

cues.text: There are more and more adenosine receptors to block.
cues.en: There are more and more adenosine receptors to block.
cues.zh: 以感受到相同的警覺 有越來越多的腺苷受體需要被阻斷

cues.text: It's also why if you suddenly quit caffeine, you may experience an unpleasant withdrawal.
cues.en: It's also why if you suddenly quit caffeine, you may experience an unpleasant withdrawal.
cues.zh: 有越來越多的腺苷受體需要被阻斷 這也是為什麼 如果你突然戒掉咖啡因 你可能會經歷一段不舒服的退癮

cues.text: With plenty of receptors and no competition, adenosine can work overtime,
cues.en: With plenty of receptors and no competition, adenosine can work overtime,
cues.zh: 你可能會經歷一段不舒服的退癮 有著許多受體，並且沒有競爭者 腺苷可能加班

cues.text: causing symptoms like headaches, tiredness, and depressed moods.
cues.en: causing symptoms like headaches, tiredness, and depressed moods.
cues.zh: 腺苷可能加班 造成症狀如頭痛 疲倦 和憂鬱的心情

cues.text: But in a few days, the extra adenosine receptors will disappear,
cues.en: But in a few days, the extra adenosine receptors will disappear,
cues.zh: 但幾天後，多餘的腺苷受體就會消失

cues.text: your body will readjust, and you'll feel just as alert as ever,
cues.en: your body will readjust, and you'll feel just as alert as ever,
cues.zh: 但幾天後，多餘的腺苷受體就會消失 你的身體會重新調整 然後你會感覺像從前一樣警覺

cues.text: even without an infusion of the world's most popular stimulant.
cues.en: even without an infusion of the world's most popular stimulant.
cues.zh: 然後你會感覺像從前一樣警覺 即使沒有注入全世界 最受歡迎的興奮劑
